intro_html: Pulled pork gets all the attention, but shredded beef holds barbecue sauce better and reheats without drying out, which makes it the smarter choice for a week of containers. The sauce is built from scratch out of ketchup, brown sugar, vinegar, and mustard, so you control the sweetness instead of a bottle deciding for you. Each bowl carries 35 grams of protein and 686 calories for about $3.24.
cost_closing_html: About $3.24 a bowl. Homemade barbecue sauce out of pantry staples costs a fraction of a bottle and tastes like you meant it.
shop_smart: Ketchup, brown sugar, cider vinegar, and mustard are the sauce. All four are long life pantry items, so buy the larger containers and stop paying the small size premium.
Chuck roast is the cut that shreds. Buy it on the sale cycle and freeze a second one, because this recipe works just as well with beef that has been frozen.
The dry rub is all spices you likely already own. Paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and cumin cost pennies per batch out of jars you keep anyway.
Green onions are a finisher, not a structural ingredient. One bunch covers the whole batch with room to spare.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Mix the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, salt, and black pepper into a rub and press it into the chuck roast on all sides.
Sear the roast in the olive oil over high heat until the rub darkens and forms a crust, then move it to the slow cooker.
Pour the beef broth into the bottom of the cooker, cover, and cook on low for 8 hours until the beef shreds under a fork.
While it cooks, whisk the ketchup, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and a shot of hot sauce together for the barbecue sauce.
Shred the beef and drain off most of the cooking liquid, leaving just enough to keep it moist.
Pour the barbecue sauce over the shredded beef, stir it through, and cook on high 30 more minutes so the sauce tightens onto the meat.
Cook the rice separately and scatter the sliced green onions over the top.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Spoon that weight of saucy beef into each container, then add the same weight of rice to every one. Each bowl lands at 686 calories with 35 grams of protein.

head.description: Slow cooker BBQ shredded beef bowls meal prep: rubbed chuck roast cooked 8 hours and tossed in a from scratch ketchup and cider vinegar sauce. 686 calories, 35g protein, about $3.24 per serving.
head.keywords: bbq shredded beef, slow cooker bbq beef, homemade bbq sauce, pulled beef bowls, budget meal prep, chuck roast recipes
steps: Rub the chuck roast with paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and cumin and sear it in olive oil.
Slow cook it on low 8 hours in beef broth until it shreds.
Whisk ketchup, brown sugar, cider vinegar, Dijon, and Worcestershire into a barbecue sauce.
Shred the beef, drain most of the liquid, add the sauce, and cook on high 30 minutes.
Cook the rice, top with green onion, and portion into 14 containers.
